diagnosis.strongest: RESP, this round. Every capture at 390 measures exactly 390px including the tutorial document that was 465px, and the fix landed as a template-derived sample (S23, 18 templates at 390 and 320) rather than a per-route patch — the widening immediately paid for itself by exposing a second live R2 break on /tutorials.
diagnosis.weakest: RESP still, at 768: /catalog keeps the 7-column table and clips it mid-label while the 390 record form goes unused. That verdict stands from the anchor and was outside this directive's scope, so nothing about it has been re-observed.
diagnosis.critical_issue: None open. Q4, the critical RESP question, moved FAIL to PASS on a measured page width; Q1, the critical TABL question, stands PASS.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: The anchor's recommendation was taken and it worked: four scoped checks (reflow, S5, S17, S18) were widened past the route lists they inherited, and all four findings closed together. The remaining move is to make that derivation structural — S23 derives its list from app/**/page.tsx, but S5, S17 and S18 still name their routes by hand, so the next new template arrives outside them again.

downstream.weakness: Three of the five fixes were only reachable because a check was widened; two of the four falsifier misses the implementer reports were defects in the CHECK, not the fix — S18 was measuring a grid-stretched box, so its 60% floor was vacuous by construction.
downstream.cause: An invariant inherits both its route list and its measurement from the verdict item that closed it, and neither is re-derived when the shape moves. A vacuous measurement reads identical to a passing one from outside.
downstream.recommendation: Hold the implementer's falsification requirement as the standing rule it has now twice earned: every clause must be shown to FIRE on a deliberate break, both signs, or it is not evidence. Pair that with route lists derived from the rendered manifest, as S23 now does, for S5, S17 and S18.
